A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EVOS and provide readable main text, equations, 17 tables, 10 figures, and Appendices A–I. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction-quality and timing experiments for image, audio, text, and 3D shape fitting, together with component ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices A–I, including reconstruction comparisons, timing measurements, and ablations.

M1.justification: Sparse fitness evaluation, frequency-guided crossover, augmented unbiased mutation, cross-frequency supervision, and selection scheduling remain unchanged. The task-specific adaptations in the appendices are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coverage: DIV2K and Kodak images, LibriSpeech audio, synthesized text images, and the Asian Dragon 3D shape. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including standard training, uniform sampling, EGRA, Expansive Supervision, Soft Mining, and INT variants. The newly cited related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Data preparation, metrics, training budgets, network configurations, sampling schedules, and testing procedures remain unchanged. The deleted repetition disclosure does not establish a change in the experimental design.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 retains the component ablations. Appendices E and G–I retain the Soft Mining analyses, scheduler and selection-ratio studies, and fitness-distribution analysis, with the same supporting evidence.

E5.justification: v2 deletes Section 4.1's statement that results were averaged across the dataset and each experiment was repeated five times. No replacement statistical reporting is provided; this establishes a reporting loss, not that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Tables 1–17 and the result figures retain their values and findings. For example, Table 2 reports the same 29.73 seconds for EVOS to reach 35 dB. No result entries, rankings, or qualitative outcomes change.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), including the selection mechanisms, loss, scheduling rule, and Appendix I distribution-change definition, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims of evolutionary sample selection, improved fitting efficiency, and approximately 48%–66% training-time reduction remain unchanged. Shortening the conclusion removes a redundant method recap without changing the contributions.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the sample-weighting interpretation, explanations of baseline behavior, and qualifications concerning low selection ratios and disabling crossover for SDF fitting. No substantive interpretation or limitation changes.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit project and source-code hyperlinks on its first page. v1 mentions released code in Appendix F without providing these links. Hardware, hyperparameters, and implementation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Shi et al. on inductive gradient adjustment and Zhang et al. on symmetric power transformation, becoming references 48 and 64 in v2. Existing references and EVOS's positioning against sampling methods are retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments, lightly edits evaluation prose, and shortens the conclusion. The section organization and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliations and project-link line shift first-page content, and the shortened conclusion fits entirely on page 8. Figures and tables retain their designs, content, and numbering; remaining layout differences are limited text reflow.

improvement.justification: Explicit project/code links and two relevant references improve access information and context. However, v2 removes the only disclosure of dataset averaging and five experimental repeats, weakening statistical transparency while retaining identical evidence. These opposing reproducibility changes leave the net quality effect uncertain from the PDFs alone.
